name: Eiffel Tower
description: An iron lattice tower standing 330 m tall, built in 1889 as the centerpiece of a World's Fair.

name: Louvre Museum
description: The world's largest art museum, housed in a former royal palace with a famous glass pyramid entrance.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel
description: A medieval abbey crowning a rocky tidal island, accessible on foot only when the sea retreats.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: A lavish 17th-century royal palace renowned for its Hall of Mirrors and sprawling formal gardens.

name: Colosseum
description: An ancient amphitheater completed in 80 AD that could hold up to 80,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
description: A freestanding marble bell tower famous worldwide for its pronounced unintentional tilt.

name: Venice Canals
description: A unique city built on 118 small islands, navigated by gondolas along a network of canals.

name: Sistine Chapel
description: A chapel ceiling painted between 1508 and 1512, depicting scenes from Genesis in breathtaking detail.

name: Amalfi Coast
description: A dramatic coastline dotted with colorful cliffside villages overlooking a deep blue sea.

name: Pompeii
description: An ancient city frozen in time when a volcanic eruption buried it under ash nearly 2,000 years ago.

name: Great Wall
description: A series of fortifications stretching over 21,000 km, built across centuries to guard ancient kingdoms.

name: Forbidden City
description: A vast imperial palace of nearly 1,000 buildings, home to 24 emperors over six centuries.

name: Terracotta Army
description: Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers buried to guard an ancient emperor's tomb in the afterlife.

name: Li River
description: A scenic river winding between dramatic limestone karst peaks, a classic subject of ancient painting.

name: Potala Palace
description: A 13-storey palace at 3,700 m altitude, once the winter residence of a revered spiritual leader.

name: Taj Mahal
description: A white marble mausoleum completed in 1653 by a Mughal emperor as an eternal tribute to his beloved wife.

name: Red Fort
description: A massive red sandstone fortress that served as the main residence of Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years.

name: Hampi Ruins
description: The scattered ruins of a once-great medieval empire — temples, bazaars and royal pavilions across a boulder landscape.

name: Angkor Wat
description: The world's largest religious monument, a 12th-century temple complex rising from the Southeast Asian jungle.

name: Borobudur
description: A 9th-century Buddhist temple pyramid decorated with over 2,500 relief panels and 500 Buddha statues.

name: Bali Rice Terraces
description: Ancient stepped rice paddies carved into hillsides, maintained by a traditional irrigation system over 1,000 years old.

name: Prambanan
description: A 9th-century Hindu temple compound of towering ornate spires, abandoned after an earthquake and reclaimed by jungle.

name: Machu Picchu
description: A 15th-century Inca citadel set on a mountain ridge more than 2,400 m above sea level, unknown to outsiders until 1911.

name: Nazca Lines
description: Enormous geoglyphs of animals etched into a desert plateau, visible only from the air and still unexplained.

name: Chichen Itza
description: A pre-Columbian archaeological site featuring the iconic El Castillo step pyramid, aligned with solar events.

name: Teotihuacan
description: An ancient city once among the world's largest, famous for its towering pyramids of the Sun and Moon.

name: Christ the Redeemer
description: A 30-metre Art Deco statue of Jesus with outstretched arms atop a mountain overlooking a vibrant coastal metropolis.

name: Amazon Rainforest
description: The world's largest tropical rainforest, covering over 5 million km² and home to roughly 10% of all species on Earth.

name: Iguazu Falls
description: A system of 275 waterfalls spanning nearly 3 km — taller and wider in volume than Niagara.

name: Perito Moreno Glacier
description: One of the world's few advancing glaciers — a 5-km-wide wall of blue ice dramatically calving into a glacial lake.

name: Pyramids of Giza
description: The only surviving wonder of the ancient world — three massive limestone tombs built over 4,500 years ago.

name: Abu Simbel
description: Two temples carved into a mountainside in the 13th century BC, later relocated to save them from rising waters.

name: Petra
description: A city of rose-red facades carved into cliff faces, once the capital of a powerful ancient trading empire.

name: Dead Sea
description: The world's saltiest large body of water — so dense that swimmers float effortlessly on its surface.

name: Burj Khalifa
description: The world's tallest building at 828 m, a gleaming skyscraper towering over a modern desert metropolis.

name: Palm Jumeirah
description: A palm-shaped artificial archipelago built in the sea, hosting luxury hotels and thousands of residences.

name: Sagrada Familia
description: A still-unfinished Gothic-inspired basilica under continuous construction since 1882, with towering sculpted facades.

name: Alhambra
description: A palatial fortress of exquisite Moorish architecture, intricate geometric tile work and serene courtyard fountains.

name: Park Güell
description: A public park of mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses and curving viaducts by a visionary modernist architect.

name: Acropolis of Athens
description: An ancient citadel atop a rocky hill, home to the Parthenon temple dedicated to a goddess of wisdom, built in 447 BC.

name: Santorini
description: A volcanic island of whitewashed cubic houses and blue-domed churches perched above a sweeping flooded caldera.

name: Meteora
description: Ancient monasteries balanced atop towering natural rock pillars rising dramatically from a wide fertile plain.

name: Big Ben
description: An iconic Gothic clock tower completed in 1859, recognized worldwide for its deep resonant bell and riverside setting.

name: Stonehenge
description: A prehistoric stone circle on a windswept plain, constructed in stages between 3000 and 1500 BC for unknown purposes.

name: Edinburgh Castle
description: A historic fortress perched on volcanic rock, dominating the skyline of a picturesque northern city of spires.

name: Giant's Causeway
description: Around 40,000 interlocking basalt columns formed by ancient volcanic activity on a rugged coastal headland.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
description: A 19th-century fairy-tale castle perched on a rugged cliff, built by a reclusive king as a personal romantic retreat.

name: Brandenburg Gate
description: An 18th-century neoclassical gate that became a potent symbol of division and later of peaceful reunification.

name: Rhine Valley Castles
description: A river valley lined with steep vineyards, medieval market towns and dozens of hilltop fortresses.

name: Hagia Sophia
description: A 6th-century domed masterpiece that has served successively as a cathedral, a mosque and a museum.

name: Cappadocia
description: A region of extraordinary volcanic rock formations, ancient cave dwellings and hot-air balloons drifting at dawn.

name: Pamukkale
description: Gleaming white terraced mineral pools cascading down a hillside, resembling a vast cotton castle from a distance.

name: Ephesus
description: One of the best-preserved ancient Mediterranean cities, featuring a grand library facade and a 25,000-seat theater.

name: Sydney Opera House
description: A sail-shaped performing arts center on a harbour, completed in 1973 and instantly recognized as an architectural icon.

name: Great Barrier Reef
description: The world's largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 km and visible from outer space.

name: Uluru
description: A colossal sandstone monolith rising 348 m from a flat red desert, sacred to the local indigenous custodians.

name: Mount Fuji
description: A perfectly symmetrical snow-capped stratovolcano — the highest peak in its country and a revered sacred mountain.

name: Fushimi Inari Shrine
description: A Shinto shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates forming tunnels winding up a forested mountain.

name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial
description: The skeletal ruins of a domed building preserved as a memorial to the world's first nuclear bomb attack in 1945.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: A colossal copper statue of a torch-bearing woman gifted in 1886, standing on an island at the entrance to a major harbor.

name: Grand Canyon
description: A vast gorge carved over millions of years, exposing nearly 2 billion years of geological history in vivid layered rock.

name: Golden Gate Bridge
description: A suspension bridge spanning a Pacific bay strait, completed in 1937 with signature orange towers often shrouded in fog.

name: Yellowstone
description: The world's first national park, home to half of all Earth's active geysers and thousands of colorful hot springs.

name: Ha Long Bay
description: A seascape of thousands of limestone islands topped with rainforest, many concealing caves and floating villages.

name: Hoi An Ancient Town
description: A remarkably intact trading port from the 15th–19th centuries, glowing with lanterns reflected in the river at night.

name: Matterhorn
description: A near-perfect pyramid-shaped peak at 4,478 m on a European border — one of the world's most photographed mountains.

name: Jungfraujoch
description: A mountain saddle at 3,454 m known as the 'Top of Europe', served by the highest railway station on the continent.

name: Hallstatt
description: A postcard-perfect lakeside village of pastel houses nestled between steep mountains and a mirror-still lake.

name: Schönbrunn Palace
description: A grand Baroque imperial palace of 1,441 rooms set in formal gardens on the edge of a Central European capital.

name: Prague Castle
description: The world's largest ancient castle complex — a silhouette of spires and towers dominating a medieval city skyline.

name: Plitvice Lakes
description: Sixteen terraced lakes linked by waterfalls shimmering in vivid shades of blue, green and grey.

name: Dubrovnik Old Town
description: A walled medieval city of limestone streets, Baroque churches and terracotta rooftops hugging a rocky sea coast.

name: Northern Lights
description: Ribbons of green, purple and pink light dancing across the Arctic sky, triggered by charged solar particles.

name: Blue Lagoon
description: A geothermal spa in a lava field, filled with milky-turquoise silica-rich water at a constant soothing temperature.

name: Table Mountain
description: A flat-topped mountain forming a dramatic natural backdrop to a coastal city at the southern tip of a continent.

name: Victoria Falls
description: One of the world's largest waterfalls — its roar and mist cloud visible from over 50 km away.

name: Serengeti Migration
description: The planet's largest land migration, with over a million wildebeest crossing open savanna in a vast annual circuit.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
description: The tallest free-standing mountain on Earth at 5,895 m, its snow-capped summit rising above equatorial plains.

name: Sahara Dunes
description: The world's largest hot desert — over 9 million km² of sand seas, rocky plateaus and ancient stone cities.

name: Marrakech Medina
description: A labyrinthine medieval city of crowded souks, spice bazaars and a central square alive with storytellers and musicians.

name: Kremlin & Red Square
description: A fortress complex at the heart of a historic capital, flanked by a vast cobblestone square and a brightly domed cathedral.

name: Lake Baikal
description: The world's deepest and oldest freshwater lake, holding roughly 20% of the planet's unfrozen surface fresh water.

name: Norwegian Fjords
description: Narrow sea inlets carved by ancient glaciers, flanked by sheer cliffs plunging thousands of metres into dark water.

name: Nyhavn
description: A 17th-century waterfront of brightly painted townhouses, old wooden vessels and outdoor cafes lining a historic canal.

name: Cliffs of Moher
description: Sheer sea cliffs rising up to 214 m along an Atlantic coast, battered by waves and home to vast seabird colonies.

name: Angel Falls
description: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 m, plunging from a tepui plateau deep in tropical jungle.

name: Salar de Uyuni
description: The world's largest salt flat — a blinding white expanse that becomes a perfect sky mirror after seasonal rains.

name: Lake Titicaca
description: The world's highest navigable lake at 3,812 m, with floating reed islands inhabited by an ancient indigenous community.

name: Galápagos Islands
description: A remote volcanic archipelago whose fearless, unique wildlife directly inspired the theory of evolution.

name: Bagan Temples
description: A plain dotted with over 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas built between the 9th and 13th centuries.

name: Sigiriya Rock
description: A 180-metre rock fortress topped with 5th-century palace ruins, surrounded by ancient water gardens.

name: Mount Everest
description: The highest mountain on Earth at 8,849 m — the ultimate mountaineering goal since its first summit in 1953.

name: Banff National Park
description: A mountain park of turquoise glacier-fed lakes, ancient ice fields and dense pine forests in the spine of a continent.

name: Niagara Falls
description: Three powerful waterfalls straddling an international border, thundering with the combined flow of four Great Lakes.

name: Tikal
description: A lost Mayan city of soaring temple pyramids whose peaks emerge above an unbroken tropical rainforest canopy.

name: Easter Island Moai
description: Nearly 1,000 monumental stone statues carved by an ancient civilization on one of the world's most remote islands.

name: Atacama Desert
description: The driest non-polar desert on Earth — alien salt flats, geysers and the clearest night skies on the planet.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
description: A labyrinth of underground chambers and chapels hand-carved from salt over 700 years of continuous mining.

name: Gamla Stan
description: One of Europe's best-preserved medieval old towns — cobblestone lanes, ochre buildings and centuries of history.

name: Chocolate Hills
description: Over 1,200 nearly perfect cone-shaped hills that turn chocolate-brown in the dry season across a vast plateau.
